records.paraphrase: Among four sibling indicators (third-house lord, brother significator, occupant and aspecting planet), two or three strong ones are said to modify siblings' numbers; a navamsa fraction gives a further younger-sibling count.
records.limitations: It distinguishes strong/weak and gendered planets. The exact counting algorithm and observed births are unverified.

records.locator: Adhyaya XII verse 20, PDF 762, printed 752; rendered source image inspected
records.paraphrase: Counts planets supplying benefic dots in third from Mars in Mars's Aṣṭakavarga, then subtracts contributors in inimical or depressed signs to forecast total siblings.
records.limitations: A source-specific list/defect; do not simply score third-house sign or raw mark count. Births vs survivors must be frozen.

records.locator: Adhyaya XII around verse 24, PDF 764, printed 754
records.paraphrase: A separate procedure averages navamsa numbers of third-house lord, Mars and third-house lord measured from Mars to estimate younger siblings.
records.limitations: Alternative to XII.20, not a complementary independent prediction; verify precise sloka number across page break.

records.paraphrase: Third-house and ascendant lords together are said to indicate fraternal affection; when strong/friendly in first or third it further predicts no division of siblings' property during life.
records.limitations: Observable relationship is separate from legal partition. Sastri's note says related verses appear in another work, title not reliably OCR read.

records.paraphrase: The fourth-house lord in eleventh, eighth or sixth respectively allegedly indicates lodging abroad, lack of owned or rented home, or accommodation with paternal relatives.
records.limitations: Location, homeownership, tenancy and kin assistance are distinct outcomes, affected by economic opportunity.

records.locator: Adhyaya XII verses 142–145, PDF 802–803, printed 792–793; inspected printed PDF803
records.paraphrase: A strong fourth lord is said to favor acquisition; adverse configurations predict loss or dilapidated property, versus a strong angular/trinal fourth lord predicting a colorful or comfortable house.
records.limitations: Keep positive, negative and condition/deterioration outcomes together rather than picking an easy fit.

records.locator: Adhyaya XIII verse 43, PDF 828, printed 818; rendered page inspected
records.paraphrase: The translated text associates fifth-house Jupiter and specific Saturn divisional conditions with lineage continuing through an adopted son.
records.limitations: Adoption is culturally and legally contextual and requires voluntary independent reporting. Do not profile private kinship as factual.

records.locator: Adhyaya XIII verse 44, PDF 828, printed 818; rendered page inspected
records.paraphrase: Mars rising with Sun in eighth/fourth under benefic aspect is said to indicate a son arriving later in life.
records.limitations: Neither 'late' nor pregnancy outcome has calibrated timing; historical sex/gender assumptions and medical implications unsuitable for advice.

records.paraphrase: Fifth/ninth from Jupiter, Moon and Lagna plus lord-of-house daśā/bhukti and Jupiter transit/asterism counting are presented as alternative periods when a child may arrive.
records.limitations: Different formulas and their output windows must be frozen independently; no improvement claims based on known childbirth dates.

records.paraphrase: Ninth-house debilitated/enemy/combust bodies are associated with adversity, yet the same verse says a malefic in exaltation, own or friendly sign can instead produce good results.
records.limitations: Qualified source itself resists blanket positive/negative sign rule; historically moralized labels not person-level judgments.

records.locator: Adhyaya XIV note preceding verse 66, PDF 889, printed 879
records.paraphrase: The editor explicitly states that verses 65–87 also occur in an earlier treatise, but the printed Devanagari title is not yet confidently read.
records.limitations: Do not invent work title from OCR and do not multiply cross-book passages as independent witnesses.

records.paraphrase: Planetary conditions on ninth house distinguish worldly power and learned pursuits from adverse configurations when Mercury/Jupiter are absent, with translator source notes.
records.limitations: The absence is part of source predicate; extremely bundled outcome lists and some sensitive claims excluded.

records.locator: Lesson 2 'Kalachakra: Ten Karmic Directions', PDF 41 and 44
records.paraphrase: Rath describes eight compass-plane directions plus vertical up/down, assigning planetary influences and mythic guardians, citing BPHS 2.3 and Shiva-related literature.
records.limitations: Rath conceptual frame is not a literal Jaimini sutra, and mythic claims are not measurable physical causation.

records.paraphrase: Rath assigns directional strength from either Lagna or Arudha Lagna; Mercury/Jupiter first, Moon/Venus fourth, Saturn seventh, Sun/Mars tenth, with node analogues.
records.limitations: The Arudha extension is separately Rath's research, not unambiguous original BPHS. Define directional strength and house model before code.

records.paraphrase: For two already known charts, Rath interprets Lagna-relative digbala for profession and Arudha-relative digbala for physical direction of relocation; a Singapore account is described as having been predicted.
records.limitations: No retained prediction timestamp, neutral cases or prospective scoring in source. Do not count named Singapore story as independently successful forecast.

records.paraphrase: Rath recommends avoiding certain daily planetary periods for work in directions associated with their obstructing planets, and provides profession labels.
records.limitations: Electing time for an action is distinct from birth-derived prediction; no controlled evidence of efficacy.

records.paraphrase: Rath retells a spiritual teacher's father having a dream before conception and an alleged precise forecast of a temple stone falling, received through a loose Oriya translation.
records.limitations: No contemporaneous time-stamped original prediction, independent event certificate or held-out test is supplied in these pages. Not measured predictive accuracy.

records.paraphrase: Rath describes mantra recitations, nyasa and named ritual steps and quotes religious Sanskrit texts.
records.limitations: Practical prescription or religious practice is not evidence of chart-derived behavior or a literal Jaimini sutra.

records.paraphrase: Rath presents mantra selection tied to planet ruling the ascendant, alongside a quotation of the Surya Upanishad, and claims benefits from sunrise recitation.
records.limitations: Requires precise natal lagna and selected school; causal/effectiveness claims about mantra not independently tested.

records.paraphrase: Rath distinguishes name at birth from occupational title and gives Sanskrit phoneme examples for computing a Hamsa seed, with special handling of compound initial syllables.
records.limitations: Inputs include native-language pronunciation, birth name, and title status—not birth chart alone; no proof names alter soul or external events.

records.paraphrase: Rath recounts a dramatic prediction that a royal prince would die when struck by a boar, allegedly fulfilled by a mounted boar's head falling.
records.limitations: Legend is not independent historical forecast validation: no dated pre-event prediction document, adversarial countercases, or original chronicle verified in this packet.

method: Selected underindexed Jataka XII–XIV passages and Rath lessons 2,6,10 from exact SHA-256 matched upload PDFs. Data are historical source paraphrases, not independent observations.
